## The question

[Underbraces are ruined by mathtools (and maybe unicode-math?). How do I keep both?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/552864/underbraces-are-ruined-by-mathtools-and-maybe-unicode-math-how-do-i-keep-bot), asked by [Iris](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/121289/iris) on TeX Stack Exchange (2020-07-09; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> In writing my thesis (using XeLaTeX) I use multiple math-related packages, all for different reasons. Since introducing unicode-math and mathtools, the underbraces I applied earlier are ruined. I included unicode-math to get proper bold math symbols (I'm using `\symbfit{}`) and I included mathtools for the `\vdotswithin{}` command. One example of a ruined underbrace in my thesis is:
>
> [![Underbrace in thesis report][q-1]][q-1]
>
> All other underbraces look more or less like this. I created the same equation in a MWE. I realise the MWE could be even more minimal by writing a more minimal equation, but I think it is minimal and clear enough to illustrate the problem and in this way, the equation is the same as in my thesis. I left in the physics package and the `\pqty{}` command to verify that this is not the cause of my problem:
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{amsmath}
> \usepackage{physics}
> \usepackage{unicode-math}
> \usepackage{mathtools}
>
> \newcommand{\bi}[1]{\symbfit{#1}}
>
> \begin{document}
> $\underbrace{q\pqty{\bi{x}}}_{\text{R-density}}\qquad\qquad\underbrace{p\qty(\bi{x},\bi{y})}_{\text{G-density}} = \underbrace{p\pqty{\bi{y}|\bi{x}}}_{\text{likelihood}}\underbrace{p\pqty{\bi{x}}}_{\text{prior}}$
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> In both the thesis and the MWE, I get these warnings:
>
> > Using \overbracket and \underbracket from(unicode-math) `mathtools'
> > package.
> > 
> > I'm going to overwrite the following commands(unicode-math) from the
> > `mathtools' package:(unicode-math)(unicode-math) \dblcolon, \coloneqq,
> > \Coloneqq, \eqqcolon.
>
> When I don't include the mathtools package, I don't get the warning. In the MWE, the underbraces look fine in both cases, despite the warning:
>
> [![Underbraces in MWE][q-2]][q-2]
>
> I've also excluded mathtools in my thesis, which gives me back the underbraces. However, I then cannot use `\vdotswithin{}` in an entirely different part of my thesis. Is there a solution that allows me to use the underbraces, bold math from unicode-math and `\vdotswithin{}` from mathtools? Or another solution that gives me these (or similar results)?
>
> EDIT: After some comments I realised my MWE doesn't use the .cls file that my thesis report does. When I change the documentclass in the MWE, I can reproduce the problem (like in the first image). Not including the mathtools package then again `solves' the problem. The .cls for my thesis uses the Cambria font for math.. I don't know if the font is the problem, since the underbraces work fine without the mathtools package.

Google brought me here and Lars' comment helped me solve the problem. Just so that the question has an answer:

1. Make sure the `mathtools` package is loaded before `unicode-math`. Usually that means putting the `\usepackage{mathtools}` line in the preamble before `\usepackage{unicode-math}` or before any package that requires it. The log file will tell you when one package loads another. If `unicode-math` is loaded by your *class* file, you can put `\RequirePackage{mathtools}` before `\documentclass{…}` and the packages will still be loaded in the right order.
2. That's it. It doesn't seem the saving and reloading of `\underbrace` is necessary (now).

Here is a minimal example showing the problem.

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\usepackage{physics}
\usepackage{unicode-math}
\setmathfont{Latin Modern Math}
\usepackage{mathtools}

\newcommand{\bi}[1]{\symbfit{#1}}

\begin{document}
$\underbrace{q\pqty{\bi{x}}}_{\text{R-density}}\qquad\qquad\underbrace{p\qty(\bi{x},\bi{y})}_{\text{G-density}} = \underbrace{p\pqty{\bi{y}|\bi{x}}}_{\text{likelihood}}\underbrace{p\pqty{\bi{x}}}_{\text{prior}}$
\end{document
```

In this version, you get the ruined underbraces as in the OP's image. If you swap the loading of the two packages, everything works fine. You do get one warning:

```
Package unicode-math Warning: Using \overbracket and \underbracket from `mathtools' package. Use \Uoverbracket and \Uunderbracket for original `unicode-math' definition.
```

It seems that similarly, `\underbrace` isn't disturbed by `unicode-math`. 

If you use `unicode-math` *without `\setmathfont`*, it also works fine in either order. And I believe that's because the default math font (Latin Modern Math) isn't loaded until `\begin{document}`. In that situation, it does happen after `mathtools` is loaded.
